Simulate Experiments With a Known Third-Variable Role

simulate_role_data.Rd

Generates a randomized experiment with a binary treatment X, a third variable measured before (Z_pre) and after (Z_post) treatment with measurement error, and an outcome Y, in one of six worlds whose true role is known.

Usage

simulate_role_data(
  world = c("neither", "moderator", "mediator", "curved_mediator", "cancelling", "both"),
  n = 400,
  me = 0.3,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

world

One of the six worlds above.

n

Sample size (even). Treatment is completely randomized, n/2 per arm.

me

Standard deviation of the measurement error in each wave of \(Z\). Default 0.3.

seed

Optional seed.

Value

A data frame with columns X, Z_pre, Z_post, Y, and attributes world and truth.

Details

The six worlds:

"neither"

Treatment does not move \(Z\); \(Z\) affects \(Y\) but does not modify the effect of \(X\).

"moderator"

Baseline \(Z\) modifies the effect of \(X\); treatment does not move \(Z\).

"mediator"

Treatment moves \(Z\), which affects \(Y\) linearly.

"curved_mediator"

As "mediator" with a convex \(Z \to Y\) effect, which makes baseline \(Z\) a genuine effect modifier: the true role is "both".

"cancelling"

Treatment moves \(Z\) up for some units and down for others, the units it moves up benefit more, and baseline \(Z\) modifies nothing: not a moderator.

"both"

Treatment moves \(Z\) and baseline \(Z\) modifies the effect.

See also

role_test, role_simulation

Examples

head(simulate_role_data("cancelling", n = 200, seed = 1))
#>   X      Z_pre      Z_post          Y
#> 1 1  0.3699207  0.58725067  2.0750806
#> 2 0 -0.4376004 -0.03467079 -0.1434375
#> 3 0 -0.9648468 -0.64224481 -0.9218453
#> 4 1 -0.3519595  0.82080141  0.6816605
#> 5 0 -1.3126439 -2.98953246 -0.8257504
#> 6 1  0.5554119  1.68980644  0.5397130
